methodology: Scope
Read-only corpus-wide MK study
Table 1
Every explicitly MK-annotated node; actual annotation IDs retained, including missing IDs and placeholders.
Observed annotations
Table 2
One row per component within each distinct attested structure/lemma variant, plus separately labeled literal dictionary definitions; never one row per text occurrence.
Parent paths and order preserve hierarchy. Repeated MK frequencies must not be summed across component rows.
Table 3
Aggregate Table 1 by MK form, target form/ID and selection type; counts sum to Table 1.
Two selection types remain separate.
Table 4
Exact same-string textual occurrences lacking an MK node over that exact span; candidate inventory, not a missing-annotation error list.
Substrings inside larger terminals/words and larger MK expressions are retained with explicit notes.
Matching
Exact, case-sensitive continuous transcription over each whole Text, across existing source-line boundaries; overlapping positions counted once each. No different spelling/inflection equivalences.
Deduplication key: corpus file, Text ordinal, character start/end, MK form.
MK frequency
Number of explicitly annotated MK occurrences of the exact realized form.
Distinct from total-string, lemma and MK–target counts.
Total occurrences
Every exact continuous-string match, including MK and non-MK contexts.
Individual forms can overlap or be nested; totals across different forms are not unique corpus-token counts.
Lemma frequency
Distinct (Text, exact character span, lemma ID) occurrences, including internal and terminal annotations.
Missing IDs have blank frequencies; unknown/missing is not zero.
Target rule
Temporary operational assumption for this statistical study only: first following reliably identified head/content word, skipping grammatical/function items; otherwise immediately following word.
Not an established linguistic/corpus rule. No project policy, annotation or data has been changed.
Target granularity
Whole existing word-level groups from current project segmentation, not invented component/head splits.
Original tags, dictionary annotations and source context remain available for review.
Head/content selection

Supported nominal, verbal, adjectival, adverbial or numeral word groups; documented grammatical categories are skipped. A pronominal genitive modifier is bypassed only where the existing tree exposes a unique following nominal head.
Unclear categories or head evidence trigger immediate-word fallback; no semantic MK→target link is asserted.
Target-selection types
head/content-word heuristic; immediate-word fallback; no following word.
Selections/evidence are explicit and separate in Table 3. Blank-target counts record unassigned MK occurrences, not associations with a known target.
Source lines
Existing ordered source-marker/raw-text segments, numbered from 1. No metrical or poetic divisions reconstructed.
Following-line context is blank at the last source line; no-source-marker cases are explicitly marked unavailable.
Spanning matches
Record both start and end source-line numbers. Following-line fields use the line after the ending source line.
Containing-line source field shows all matched source lines in order; no word-level kanji substring is inferred.
Meanings
Dictionary MEANING values, with GLOSS used only if no MEANING is available. Missing annotations/meanings are not invented.

Table 3 preserves actual attested IDs, including placeholders. Table 4 known specific IDs come from explicit MK annotations or exact dictionary FORM entries labeled makura kotoba; L099999 is not a form-specific identification.
Components
Attested tree nodes, including phrase wrappers and hierarchy, are distinct from writing-mode parts. Dictionary COMPOUND references are separately labeled and remain literal.
Dictionary-only rows do not prove occurrence-level decomposition or resolve incomplete/self-referential definitions.
Gojūon order
Matching dictionary FORM/KANA pairs where available; otherwise the project phonemic_to_kana converter. Japanese ja-JP collation; reliable kana groups first, unreliable keys last.
The same MK group order is used in all four tables.
Snapshot
All outputs are fixed derived research tables, not live importers or editable frequency models.
Recorded hashes and source locations are in the accompanying investigation evidence.
Source corpus
data/txt/text; data/txt/trees; data/xml/text; data/xml/trees
115 TXT/XML document pairs, 5,665 Texts.
Dictionary
data/txt/dict/dictionary.txt; data/xml/dict/dictionary.xml
Complete parsed field maps verified equal.
Validation
Independent TXT parse and in-memory conversion match all MK forms/IDs per Text; terminal material and all source-line rows agree between TXT and stored XML.
No source files regenerated or changed on disk.
Reconciliation
1891 explicit MK rows; 1334 candidate rows; 1891 aggregate MK–target count.
MK + non-MK counts reconcile separately for every form; lemma counts use corpus-wide IDs, not surface spelling.
Research limitations
Targets are operational estimates, not confirmed linguistic relationships. Unassigned and placeholder MK IDs and dictionary/tree differences require review.
See the new MK-study investigation report; existing issue registers have not been changed.
